text: For the choirmaster. According to mahalath. A maskil of David. [Footnote: "Mahalath" and "maskil" are Hebrew terms of uncertain meaning; "mahalath" is probably a melody or musical setting, and "maskil" a type of psalm, perhaps a contemplative or instructive song.]

versions.text: For the choirmaster. According to mahalath. A maskil of David.
versions.explanation: Two transliterated Hebrew terms appear in a single short line with no explanation. A brief footnote helps hearers and readers who will not recognize either word, without disrupting the oral flow of the superscription.

text: The fool says in his heart, "There is no God." They are corrupt, their deeds are vile; no one does good.
God looks down from heaven on the children of men to see if anyone has understanding, if anyone seeks God.

versions.text: God looks down from heaven on the children of Adam to see if anyone has understanding, if anyone seeks God.
versions.explanation: בְּנֵי אָדָם here is the generic idiom for humankind rather than a reference to the individual Adam. Rendering it "children of Adam" may lead hearers to think of a specific genealogy; "children of men" (or "the human race") keeps the universal scope the psalm requires.

text: All have turned away, together they have grown rotten; no one does good, not even one.
Do they know nothing, these evildoers, who devour my people as they devour bread, who never call on God?
There they were seized with terror where there was nothing to fear, for God scattered the bones of those who besieged you. You put them to shame, for God rejected them.
Oh, that salvation for Israel would come out of Zion! When God restores the fortunes of his people, let Jacob rejoice and Israel be glad.
